title: Can I SURVIVE Drawback Chess?
summary: Drawback Chess (drawbackchess site) vs online humans. Each player gets a random secret drawback; goal is 3 wins, and a win only counts if his drawback is harder than the opponent's. Game 1 (black): his drawback Pawn Battle (lose if you have fewer pawns than the opponent) - he sacs a piece for a pawn early and wins; opponent had True Gentleman. Game 2: Rising Water - wins; opponent had Blinded by the Sun (can't end your turn attacking e5). Game 3 (black): Devil on Your Shoulder (a devil suggests terrible moves; disobey 7 turns in a row and you must obey on the 8th) - wins by checking the king until the opponent's Treadmill drawback makes them walk into a king capture. 3/3.
rules: Standard chess pieces/setup; each player is dealt one secret random drawback (shown with an Easy-Hard difficulty slider); the opponent's drawback is revealed only after the game.
Kings can be captured (no checkmate requirement): capturing the enemy king wins; moving into check is legal.

Drawbacks seen: Pawn Battle - lose if you have fewer pawns than your opponent. Rising Water - every 10 turns the water rises one rank from your side; you can't move pieces that are underwater or move to underwater squares. Devil on Your Shoulder - a devil suggests terrible moves; if you disobey 7 turns in a row you must obey on the 8th. True Gentleman - you can never capture a queen. Blinded by the Sun - you can't end your turn attacking e5. Treadmill - (exact text not read; forced king/piece movement implied). Lame Duck - you can't move your king.
Violating/triggering your drawback loses (e.g. having fewer pawns under Pawn Battle).
win_condition: Capture the enemy king, the opponent loses via their drawback, or on time. Video goal: 3 wins with a harder drawback than the opponent.
